newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea defector's wife under arrest - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea defector's wife under arrest - newspaper.

text.p: The wife and son of North Korea's top defector are under house arrest in the communist nation, a Japanese newspaper reported on Saturday.
The Asahi Shimbun said the wife of Hwang Jang-yop, North Korea's former top ideologue, was put under house arrest shortly after her husband's defection in Beijing last February 12.
Japanese and South Korean officials had no comment on the report which quoted sources in Beijing for the information.
After spending time in Beijing and then the Phillipines, the 74-year-old Hwang arrived in his new homeland, South Korea, in April.
The Asahi said Hwang's son, whom it did not name, tried to flee by car to China as soon as he learned of his father's defection.
But he was captured before crossing the border and put under house arrest with his mother.
The newspaper said there had been no action taken against Hwang's two daughters.

Noting that family members of defectors have traditionally been jailed at concentration camps, the Asahi said the apparent lenient treatment so far to Hwang's relatives indicated North Korean concern about United States criticism of its human rights record.
Famine-hit North Korea is negotiating with the United States and its allies over massive food aid to head off starvation after two consecutive years of record floods.
